prize_parts.citation: For the theory of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator, and its experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: Kane-Mele and Molenkamp form the cleanest theory-plus-experiment chain on the shortlist: a new invariant and a new class of matter, followed by a measured quantized edge conductance in HgTe, then more than fifteen years of independent confirmation by transport and ARPES in many materials. The interpretation is stable and the idea has spread well beyond condensed matter. It gives the single verified physical discovery at the centre that I look for, and it is well connected to electronic-structure calculations of band inversion and spin-orbit coupling. Six of eight members ranked it, and every one of them independently proposed the same trio, so the attribution is as settled as it can be for this field.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe effect that Molenkamp measured, and Zhang's death in 2018 removes him from consideration. Fu, Kane and Mele, Moore and Balents, and Hasan's ARPES work on 3D topological insulators are also left out. There is also real overlap in subject with the 2016 prize for topological phase transitions and phases of matter, which Lindroth and Mehlig have rightly raised. A citation framed around the Z2 invariant and the 2D quantum spin Hall state keeps it distinct from the Haldane-Thouless-Kosterlitz work, but a colleague could still judge that the topological story has been covered.

responses.point: Lindroth ranked B036 fifth and notes that the 2016 topological-phases prize partly covers it, so novelty relative to that prize may be questioned. She put optical lattice clocks (B025) first.
responses.response: I take the overlap seriously, but I think it is smaller than it appears. The 2016 prize rewarded topological phase transitions and integer quantum Hall-type topological order in specific models, and it did not recognise time-reversal-invariant systems, the Z2 classification, or the symmetry-protected states of real spin-orbit materials. Those came later and were measured in HgTe, Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3. I agree the citation must say this clearly. I also accept that the clocks are an excellent mature case. I regard that as a different kind of strength, a metrology advance, rather than a reason to rank it above a new state of matter.

responses.point: Kroll ranked optical lattice clocks first. They are mature and reproduced at the 1e-18 level in many labs, the work is precision-limited, and Katori with Ye is a clean two-person credit with room left after the 2005 comb prize.
responses.response: I agree that B025 has the cleanest attribution on the list and the best-confirmed performance, and I would be content to see it prized. Our difference is mostly one of weighting. I put a new organising principle for matter ahead of a measurement capability, even a transformative one. I also doubt the 2005 comb prize leaves as much room as you suggest, because Ye's JILA clocks rest heavily on comb technology. That is a reservation rather than a block, which is why I list B025 as my first alternative.

responses.point: Mehlig ranked B036 second and calls it a clean, general concept with bulk invariants guaranteeing protected boundary states. He also asks how much overlap the 2016 prize leaves and notes that Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Fu and Hasan are outside the names.
responses.response: We agree on the substance. I would answer the overlap question by pointing to the Z2 invariant and the experimental realisation in HgTe, which the 2016 prize did not cover. On the missing names, I would rather not stretch the prize to add Bernevig or Hasan. The three-person limit forces a choice, and Kane-Mele with Molenkamp is the minimum that covers the decisive theory and the first observation. I would be glad to hear whether you think the three-dimensional work shifts the balance.

responses.point: Pearce ranked IceCube first as a bold instrument achievement that opened neutrino astronomy, while deferring to colleagues on condensed matter and noting that source identification is still evolving.
responses.response: I respect the instrument achievement, and I defer to you on astroparticle physics. My concern is maturity: the diffuse flux is firm, but the source picture rests on a few candidate associations, and only two of eight members ranked B007. I would want to see broader support and a clearer account of the sources before putting it ahead of a result that has been confirmed in many materials for fifteen years.

responses.point: Olsson ranked aberration-corrected electron microscopy first as a true invention that broke the Scherzer limit and is now ubiquitous, and also placed magic-angle graphene second.
responses.response: I proposed B008 myself and ranked it sixth, so I do not dismiss it. It is a genuine invention with a clear Rose, Haider and Urban chain. My hesitation is that the prize would reward an enabling instrument whose scientific discoveries lie elsewhere, and the Krivanek claim for STEM correctors is a real complication. I share your view of B022 as a strong second choice. I place it behind B036 mainly on maturity and because the pairing mechanism is still debated.

uncertainties: How much weight the committee gives to overlap with the 2016 topological-phases prize, and whether a Z2 and HgTe citation is distinct enough.
Whether Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, or the 3D topological insulator work, should displace one of the three credited names; the experts would need to settle this.
Whether the committee would prefer a two-part prize combining a metrology or optics achievement with a condensed-matter one, which the three-person cap makes hard.
Whether magic-angle graphene (B022) will be considered mature enough soon, since the superconducting pairing mechanism is unsettled.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. None of the credited names appears among my listed co-authors or mentors, and I would flag any later link to Molenkamp, Kane or Mele for recusal discussion.
